title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a scheme on which p is locally nilpotent, and BT(S) is the category of Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups over S. To each G one attaches its contravariant Dieudonné crystal D*(G), a crystal of locally free modules on the crystalline site. Its value D*(G)_S on S is a locally free O_S-module.

The page announces a canonical filtration of D*(G)_S. Fil^1 is a locally direct-factor submodule, hence locally free of finite type, equal to ω_G. This gives the exact sequence

(*) 0 → ω_G → D*(G)_S → t_{G*} → 0.

- ω_G is the module of invariant differentials of the formal Lie group Ḡ ⊂ G attached to G (the formal completion along the zero section, to be constructed later).
- t_{G*} = ω_{G*}^∨ is the Lie algebra of the Cartier/Serre dual BT group G*.
- The sequence is functorial in G and compatible with base change along S' → S.

In modern terms this is the Hodge filtration on the (contravariant) Dieudonné crystal: Fil^1 = ω_G, with quotient Lie(G^∨). It is the BT analogue of the Hodge filtration 0 → ω_{A^∨}… on H^1_dR of an abelian scheme. In the abelian-scheme case one has D(A[p^∞])_S ≅ H^1_dR(A/S), Fil = ω_A, quotient = Lie(A^∨).

Purpose: this filtration is the ingredient of the Grothendieck–Messing deformation theorem stated on the next page. Lifts of G along a nilpotent PD thickening S' → S are equivalent to lifts of the Hodge filtration to D*(G)_{S'}. Combined with the full-faithfulness problem (Problème 1 on the previous pages), this would describe BT(S) via filtered F-V-crystals.
errors: Notational slip: the text writes 't_G = ω_{G*}^∨ est l'Algèbre de Lie associée au groupe de BT dual G*'. Consistently with the exact sequence, this should read t_{G*} = ω_{G*}^∨ (Lie algebra of G*), with t_G = ω_G^∨ the Lie algebra of G.

The existence of the formal Lie group Ḡ attached to G over a general S with p locally nilpotent is a nontrivial theorem (Grothendieck; proved in Messing's thesis), deferred here ('construit plus bas'). This is not an error, but the statement depends on it.

ideas.what: Hodge filtration ω_G ⊂ D*(G)_S with quotient Lie(G*), functorial and compatible with base change
ideas.modern_name: Hodge filtration on the Dieudonné crystal of a p-divisible group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM Nice 1970; Montréal lectures 1970, publ. 1974); construction and proofs by W. Messing (LNM 264, 1972); Mazur–Messing (LNM 370, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', Actes ICM Nice 1970; 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné', Presses Univ. Montréal 1974

ideas.what: Interpretation of the filtration as the 1-dimensional analogue of the Hodge filtration on relative de Rham cohomology (made explicit on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Comparison D(A[p^∞]) ≅ H^1_dR(A/S) respecting Hodge filtrations

ideas.what: Formal Lie group Ḡ ⊂ G associated to a BT group over a base where p is locally nilpotent
ideas.modern_name: Formal completion of a p-divisible group (Grothendieck's theorem, formal Lie group of a BT group)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft exposition of the Hodge filtration on Dieudonné crystals, which is exactly the well-known Grothendieck–Messing framework. It was announced at ICM 1970 and in the Montréal lectures, and worked out by Messing. There is no new result or connection here; only the drafting details (Fil^1 notation added by hand, a footnote) are unpublished.
